recipes.description: Current complete production wrapper, with no intervention.
Inherited short-Vww reanalysis, explicit sentence context, genuine heavy-syllable apocope, and a separately retained j-created residual.
recipes.assumptions: Bare corpus inputs explicitly select stressed phonologically-final citation context; this is an evaluation convention, not an inference from acute notation or a claim about every historical utterance. Only the independently discussed you sandhi variant selects unstressed final context. U+1D58 marks that context; U+1D9C marks unstressed nonfinal/proclitic context. These annotations specify context at SC098, not at every earlier historical event. The derived prefix carries annotations transparently outside each pre-SC098 operation, so neither root anchors nor final-z loss can be accidentally bled. SC098 consumes the stressless-final mark; it transfers the nonfinal mark to the right boundary, where it blocks finality-dependent rules through the later OE apocope corridor. AFHV applies the unchanged OE law and then removes that boundary annotation before subsequent vowel reduction and rendering. Ringe and Taylor p.58 explicitly extends the proclisis explanation to later apocope. PGmc segmental reconstructions and entry stages do not change. The representative insertion after assimilation and before j-gemination distinguishes inherited/coronal-created ww from later j-created ww without a provenance flag; it asserts no new strict historical edge. Later atomic au/eu/iu realization remains on the English branch. Singleton and contraction paths are retained. The late e/i+ww+j simplification remains a disclosed representation residual, not a newly invented historical sound law.
recipes.limitations: Private production proposal only; context migration and all canonical source/book propagation remain unadopted. Inherited geminate glides are described after short vowels (Fulk p.117); hypothetical long-Vww and oww are negative domain tests, not reconstructed PGmc positives. Parallel inherited jj is independently governed and is not reopened. The uww quantity uses Ringe and Taylor's preferred long-vowel account, whose shadow evidence is qualified on p.66. The boundary explanation is CAPR's existing neogrammarian working account; Ringe and Taylor also hedge about variation. Staged and/umbi tests select the source's proposed sandhi contexts and do not prove historical context assignments. No corpus admissions.
